# Azoic tutorial series

A **technical tariff** estimates expected claim cost before expenses, commission,
profit, taxes, and other commercial loadings. For policy $i$:

- **exposure** is the insured time at risk and is the modelling weight;
- **frequency** is expected claims per exposure unit;
- **severity** is expected cost per claim, fitted only where claims occurred;
- **pure premium** is expected claim cost per exposure unit, either modelled
  directly or as frequency × severity.

This series uses the French freMTPL2 portfolio because one dataset supports
direct Tweedie, frequency–severity, preprocessing, diagnostics, tariff export,
reporting, tuning, and experiment tracking. The
[Swedish motorcycle study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13385-021-00264-3)
is a useful methodological reference, but is narrower and is not duplicated on
purpose.

## What to read first

You should be comfortable with Python DataFrames and the idea of fitting a model
on training data and evaluating it on separate data. Exposure, claim counts,
claim costs, and pure-premium units are defined above; no MLflow or tuning
experience is needed for the main path. The experiment chapter introduces GLMs,
GBMs, and the log link before their settings. The main path fits only a direct
GLM and a raw-feature GBM; the structured teacher enters at optional distillation
and tuning. For a smaller first step, run the
[network-free first-model guide](https://thomasbury.github.io/azoic/getting-started/first-model/)
with synthetic data before this full real-data book.

| Main path | Practical question |
|---|---|
| [Portfolio](01-portfolio.qmd) | What population and loss layer am I pricing? |
| [Experiments](02-experiments.qmd) | How do I fit comparable candidates safely? |
| [Essential diagnostics](03-diagnostics.qmd) | Where do predictions rank and calibrate well? |
| [Scoring and tariff](04-scoring-tariff.qmd) | How do I score policies and review an export? |

**First stopping point:** after outcome-free scoring, you can produce expected
claim rates and convert them to policy costs using exposure. **Second stopping
point:** after tariff review, you can explain the workbook's factors, prediction
scale, and held-out limitations. GBM distillation is an optional extension within
that chapter; the direct GLM already exports a multiplicative tariff.

Choose later recipes only when needed: [reporting and operations](05-reporting-mlops.qmd),
[frequency–severity](06-frequency-severity.qmd), [tuning](07-tuning.qmd),
[period diagnostics](08-temporal-stability.qmd),
[protected-group review](09-protected-group.qmd), or
[manual factor revisions](10-manual-tariff.qmd).

## Execution and tutorial helpers

Every chapter runs in a fresh kernel and fits its own models. No chapter needs a
workbook, report, or fitted estimator from an earlier chapter. The shared loader
reuses its cleaned data cache and regenerates the sampled portfolio parquet;
reports and workbooks are outputs, not chapter prerequisites. A sequential book
render checks the full sequence but cannot by itself prove that each chapter
works with only its declared inputs.

`load_portfolio`, `make_experiment_configs`, `holdout_diagnostics`, and
`setup_mlflow_tracking` are **tutorial helpers**, not public Azoic functions.
Their source and the editable sample/claim-cap constants live in
[`examples/_shared.qmd`](https://github.com/ThomasBury/azoic/blob/main/examples/_shared.qmd).
Shared imports and helper definitions execute silently; chapter cells show the
steps relevant to the lesson. See the [cache contract](01-portfolio.qmd#cache-and-sample-controls)
before changing the loss layer or sample.

## Setup

Install the tutorial stack from a checkout and render the book with `just demo`:

```bash
uv sync --group demo --extra mlops --extra plot --extra tune
quarto --version
OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 just demo
```

The thread limits keep numerical libraries from competing for all available
cores during repeated fits. For one chapter, for example:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  uv run quarto render examples/05-reporting-mlops.qmd
```

Quarto executes the Python cells and assembles the chapters into HTML. Install
its [CLI separately](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) before running the commands above; `uv sync` installs the
Python tutorial dependencies, not Quarto itself. Run from the repository root
with `uv`, `just`, and Quarto available on your PATH.

Quarto is an external system prerequisite. The render fetches pinned OpenML
datasets, so this is the only onboarding path that needs network access. Only
the tutorial sources are committed; fetched data, caches, workbooks, reports,
MLflow state, and the generated book stay under ignored
`examples/_artifacts/` and `examples/_book/`.

This is historical capped-layer modelling, not a final commercial price. Large
losses, claims development, inflation, commercial loadings, and deployment need
separate decisions. Once the displayed holdout influences a revision, assess that
revision on fresh evaluation data; see the
[operational boundaries](05-reporting-mlops.qmd#operational-boundaries).
